narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and the assessment found that your overall credit profile carries enough risk that the application could not be approved at this time. The model estimated a 50% probability that you represent a bad credit risk — essentially a coin flip — which, while not a definitive verdict on your financial character, was just enough to tip the decision toward denial given the combination of factors in your profile.

The single most influential factor working against your application was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, only about 1 in 5 had a negative checking account balance, while the majority either had no checking account or maintained a positive balance. A negative balance signals to the model that you may already be under financial strain, making it harder to take on additional debt responsibly.

On a more positive note, the duration of your requested loan — 12 months — actually worked in your favor. Approved applicants took out loans lasting nearly 20 months on average, so your shorter repayment period suggests a more modest and manageable commitment, and the model recognized this as a lower-risk signal.

However, the purpose of your loan — purchasing a new car — added some pressure back toward the denial. While new car purchases are not uncommon among approved applicants (about 1 in 5 approved loans were for this purpose), this category carries slightly more risk in the model's assessment compared to purposes like buying a used car or financing household electronics, and it contributed modestly to the unfavorable outcome.

Beyond these top three factors, your profile has some additional characteristics worth noting. Your credit history includes past payment delays, which places you in a group representing fewer than 9% of approved applicants — most of whom had a clean or critical-but-resolved repayment record. Your installment rate of 4% of disposable income is also higher than the approved applicant average of about 2.94%, meaning a larger share of your income would go toward repayments, which adds financial pressure. You also have two existing credits at this bank, compared to an average of 1.42 among approved applicants, and two financially dependent people, compared to an average of just over one.

Given all of this, the most actionable steps you can take are to work toward bringing your checking account into a positive balance and, if possible, addressing any outstanding payment delays to improve your credit history. Reducing your existing debt obligations before reapplying would also strengthen your profile considerably. You may also want to consider requesting a smaller loan amount or exploring whether a co-applicant or guarantor could support your application, as these factors can meaningfully shift the risk assessment in your favor.
